styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Faisal Mosque, Saidpur village and the city's museums.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Margalla Hills trails, viewpoints and Daman-e-Koh.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Taxila ruins and old Rawalpindi, an hour away.

stays.why: Central business strip; easy taxi and Metro Bus access to most sights.
Leafy, walkable sectors with cafés, restaurants and upscale hotels near the Margalla foothills.
Good-value guesthouses and small hotels; close to Blue Area and the Metro Bus line.
Quiet, green and close to Faisal Mosque and the Margalla road; best for hill views.

food: Try Pakistani classics: chicken karahi, seekh kebabs, haleem and biryani. Portions are big; share.
Look for a local 'food street' area for grilled meat and parathas in the evening; ask your hotel which is closest.
Melt-in-mouth nihari and halwa puri are traditional breakfasts; go early before they sell out.
Vegetarians are well served: daal, chana, saag and paneer dishes are on most menus.
Tap water is not safe to drink. Stick to bottled or filtered water, and skip ice if unsure.
more_time: Add a half-day to Taxila's UNESCO ruins and museum, roughly an hour northwest by car.
Cross into old Rawalpindi for Raja Bazaar and the bazaars around Murree Road; go with a local or a guide.
In summer, head up to Murree or the Galyat hills for cooler air; check road conditions on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights cover Faisal Mosque, a Margalla Hills walk and a Taxila or Rawalpindi half-day without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold days around 16°C and chilly nights near 6°C. Pack a warm layer.
February: mild and dry-ish; good for walking the Margalla trails.
March: pleasant spring, but expect about 11 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
April: warm and comfortable, around 29°C highs. A great month for sightseeing.
May: heating up to 34°C. Do outdoor sights early morning.
June: hot, highs near 36°C. Plan indoor sights at midday.
July: monsoon starts; about 20 rain days and humid nights. Keep plans flexible.
August: still wet and humid, around 19 rain days. Carry an umbrella.
September: rain eases; warm and green. Good for hills and viewpoints.
October: dry and comfortable, around 29°C. One of the best months to visit.
November: cool and clear, highs near 22°C. Excellent for walking and ruins.
December: crisp and cold, highs around 18°C. Layer up for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Four clear seasons: cool dry winters, a hot pre-monsoon spring, a wet humid monsoon in July–August, and a dry pleasant autumn.

items.title: Best time: October to April
items.text: Mild to cool days and low rain. Ideal for Faisal Mosque, Taxila and the Margalla trails.

items.title: Hot before the monsoon (May–June)
items.text: Highs of 34–36°C. Sightsee early morning and rest at midday.

items.title: Monsoon in July–August
items.text: About 19–20 rain days a month and humid nights. Short heavy showers; keep plans flexible.

items.title: Spring showers
items.text: March has about 11 rain days. A light rain jacket helps on hill walks.

items.title: Cold winter nights
items.text: January lows near 6°C and December near 7°C. Bring a warm jacket for evenings.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Modest, breathable clothing; sturdy shoes for trails; a warm layer in winter; sun protection year-round.

transit.best: Ride apps or taxis for most trips; the Metro Bus is cheap for the Islamabad–Rawalpindi run.

modes.text: Metro Bus red line links Islamabad with Rawalpindi Saddar; a single ticket is about Rs 30. The Orange line shuttle runs from the airport parking lot (row 22) to the Metro network for about Rs 90.
Blue and green bus lines use a separate ticketing system and run on regular roads.
Taxis are plentiful; agree the fare first, roughly Rs 200 per sector. Careem and InDrive are the local favourite; Careem Bike is cheapest.
Car hire with driver is easy. Useful for Taxila, Murree and hill trips.
Pleasant in the planned sectors, but distances are long. Use a ride for anything far.
